solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: tendency at sea

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'tendency at sea (6)': the wordplay needs A + DRIFT (tendency), so a leading 'A' appears lost; a search did not recover the printed clue

clue.text: Hit man when given cheek at home

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
sass is impudence or back-talk
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A contract killer becomes one when he is lippy while staying at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional killer paid for a murder, a hit, is a murderer of this kind.

clue.text: Boarding train, first to leave in middle of night

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for train departs, leaving the rest

parts.note: to groom someone is to train or prepare them
taken as written

indicators.note: picks out the central letter of the five-letter word night

explanation.surface: Someone boards a train just as the first passenger leaves at midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodging in rented rooms is boarding, both meaning living as a paying lodger.

clue.text: Warplane circling about does for cargo ship

indicators.note: the warplane goes round, enclosing the short word for about

parts.note: a fighter is a military combat aircraft
re means about or concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: A fighter jet circles round, standing in for a cargo vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does for' is linking padding meaning 'serves as'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel built to carry goods rather than passengers is a merchant transport ship.

clue.text: Paper associated with a union?

parts.note: union here means a wedding, where small bits of coloured paper are thrown over the couple

explanation.surface: A question about paperwork connected to a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests trade unions and their documents; it is a marriage, and the paper is the scraps thrown at the newly-weds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny coloured paper pieces showered on a bride and groom are the classic wedding throw.

clue.text: Stars are so excellent

definitions.meaning: stars lie beyond our planet, literally off the Earth
an idiom for superb or wonderful

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for marvellous, and literally describes things located beyond Earth, like stars.

clue.text: Cigarette lit for gang leader

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
a fire that is lit is said to be in, still burning

explanation.surface: A gangster boss lights up a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: A fire is 'in' while still alight. Fagin leads the gang of boy pickpockets in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's villain runs a band of child thieves in Oliver Twist, making him a criminal ringleader.

clue.text: Whirlwind ripped a door half off

parts.note: something ripped is torn

indicators.note: only the first half of the four-letter word door remains

explanation.surface: A storm tore a door half off its hinges.
explanation.definitionFit: A violently rotating column of air is a twister, the most destructive kind of whirlwind.

clue.text: Designs must include large examples

indicators.note: the word for designs has to take in the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: designs in the sense of plans or ideas
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A design brief insists on big examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Models of perfection to be copied are standards or exemplars, so examples in that sense.

clue.text: Novelist heading off for estuary cut off in a place full of trees

indicators.note: the novelist's surname loses its first letter

parts.note: Christopher Isherwood, English novelist of the Berlin stories
taken as written

indicators.note: the word estuary is truncated, keeping only its first three letters

explanation.surface: A writer heads off for an estuary but is cut off somewhere wooded.
explanation.walkthrough: Sherwood Forest is the Nottinghamshire woodland of the Robin Hood legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous English woodland of Robin Hood legend is a large area thick with trees.

clue.text: Bird causing one to talk on street

indicators.note: in an across clue, the later pieces are placed on, i.e. after, the street abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
to chat is to talk

explanation.surface: Something prompts a person to strike up a conversation in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird with a call like two stones knocked together, common on heaths.

clue.text: Some buying (or selling) an evergreen shrub

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people are buying or selling a hedge plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiny yellow-flowered furze stays green all year, a classic heathland bush.

clue.text: Vocalist going about with regular partygoer?

indicators.note: the vocalist goes round the abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a vocalist is a singer

explanation.surface: A singer travels around with someone who never misses a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively person who enjoys parties and nightlife is a swinging, fashionable socialite.

clue.text: Letters to a celeb, cool and masculine, it's said

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: to fan is to cool, and masculine is male; together they sound out the answer

explanation.surface: A celebrity is described as cool and manly, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence from admirers sent to a famous person is admirers' post.

clue.text: Bar of gold I obtained around noon originally

indicators.note: the first pieces wrap round the letter from noon

parts.note: got means obtained

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of noon

explanation.surface: I picked up a gold bar around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast block of precious metal is the standard form bullion takes.

clue.text: A Jamaican port, or I choose slightly reduced rum

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, signalling the letters are mixed
the word choose loses a little, its final letter

explanation.surface: Asked about a Caribbean port, I pick a smaller measure of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' fits the Jamaican setting as the drink but is the anagram signal, meaning odd. Ocho Rios is a resort port on Jamaica's north coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The cruise-ship resort town on Jamaica's north coast is a harbour on that island.

clue.text: Protect telephone receiver

parts.note: to ring someone is to telephone them
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: A telephone handset kept safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiver' looks like part of the phone; it is a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring-fence money or assets is to guarantee they are kept safe from other use.

clue.text: Principal character in a line

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person, a character
taken as written

explanation.surface: The lead actor plays a role in a line of the script.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means chief or of the greatest importance, as in cardinal sin.

clue.text: Ambassador meeting newly-weds in British isles

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE
brides are women newly married

explanation.surface: A diplomat meets honeymooners in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' joins the pieces and 'in' is a link. The Hebrides are the island groups off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish archipelago off the west coast is a set of islands belonging to Britain.

clue.text: Speak fast

definitions.meaning: to put thoughts into words, to voice them
as an adjective, describing a train or delivery that is rapid

explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is this verb, and a speedy train or post service carries the same word.

clue.text: Operatic heroine common? Not quite

indicators.note: the word for common falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: normal means common or ordinary

explanation.surface: A typical opera heroine is almost ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: Norma is the druid priestess of Bellini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini's druid priestess gives her name to the opera, so she is its title role.

clue.text: Race around on hill — that generates energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the hill
the letters of race are turned around into a new order

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Runners race around a hilltop power station.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear plant's core vessel produces power by fission, so it is an energy source.

clue.text: Genius is reportedly in charge

indicators.note: the spoken word goes inside the word for charge

parts.note: a ward is a person in someone's charge

indicators.note: is spoken aloud sounds like the letters IZ

parts.note: the word as said aloud

explanation.surface: A brilliant mind is said to be the one running things.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard at something is a person of exceptional skill, so a gifted expert.

clue.text: I am finished with old painting technique

parts.note: contracted to I'm
past means over or finished

explanation.surface: I'm done with an outdated way of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying oil paint thickly so brush strokes stand out is a recognised artist's method.

clue.text: Southern shopping centre, limited in size

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A shopping centre in the south is not very big.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of modest dimensions is being little.

clue.text: Casual worker, not switched on at first

indicators.note: the switched-off piece comes first, before the worker

parts.note: a device not switched on is off
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: An idle labourer who has not yet got going.
explanation.definitionFit: Being casual or curt in manner is offhand, showing little attention or care.

clue.text: District housing new stadium

indicators.note: the district contains the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: an area is a district

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood is home to a new sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed space for sport or entertainment surrounded by seating is a venue of this kind.

clue.text: Duke, duke wife's divorced

indicators.note: the wife is separated off, removed from the title

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington, victor of Waterloo
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A duke's wife has left him.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Duke' is Duke Ellington, the jazz bandleader, whose title was a nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The jazz composer Edward Kennedy Ellington was known by the nickname Duke.

clue.text: Fail to keep backing during meeting, being without friends?

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed within the meeting

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting

indicators.note: the word for fail to keep is read backwards

parts.note: to lose something is to fail to keep it

explanation.surface: Someone loses heart during a meeting, feeling friendless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word; the definition is playful, since desolate means bleak and forlorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate describes feeling lonely and abandoned, as someone with no companions might.

clue.text: Unreal shot of the nervous system

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, signalling the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An imaginary image of the body's nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to nerves or the nervous system.
